p2.title: PNG/geometry check in load_snapshot is gated fail-open on an unnormalized key
p2.lines: load_snapshot: evidence_rows = {row["image"]: row ...}; later `if name in evidence_rows:`
p2.detail: Asset names come from _evidence_files via _relative_name(row["image"]). The lookup map is keyed on the raw row["image"]. If _relative_name performs any normalization (leading './', backslashes, case), the asset name will not be in evidence_rows and _check_evidence_image is silently skipped for that PNG. build_service_review.py has the same key mismatch but fails closed with KeyError, which is at least safe.
p2.minimal_fix: Gate on the validated set instead: `if name in evidence_files: _check_evidence_image(raw, evidence_rows[name], evidence_schema)` so a key mismatch raises rather than skips. Better: have _evidence_files return `{normalized_name: row}` and use that in both callers.

p2.title: Wrong-frame risk: ffmpeg select ordinal is never cross-checked against the ffprobe PTS index
p2.lines: extract_context: expression = "+".join(f"eq(n\\,{frame['ordinal']})" ...); only count and dimensions are verified afterwards
p2.detail: Frame identity relies on the assumption that select's `n` (filtergraph input frame counter) equals the ordinal from ffprobe -show_frames. Both are presentation order from the same decoder, so this normally holds, but any divergence (decoder dropping a damaged frame before -xerror fires, differing decoder thread/error-concealment behaviour) would produce an image labeled with a PTS it does not have, and the audit, sheets, and sidecar would all agree on the wrong value. The synthetic test uses a fake ffmpeg so this is untested.
p2.minimal_fix:
Append `,showinfo` to the -vf chain, run ffmpeg at `-v info`, parse the `Parsed_showinfo ... n: pts:

` lines from stderr, require exactly len(frames) lines whose pts list equals [f['pts'] for f in frames], and reject any other non-showinfo stderr. Alternatively use image2 `-frame_pts 1` naming and compare filenames to expected PTS.

resolved.basis: Frames are now bound by showinfo PTS, not select ordinal alone. -copyts keeps filter-input PTS in the stream clock, the config time_base must equal the probed one exactly, and (n, pts) must equal enumerate(frames) exactly. -loglevel level+info plus the [warning|error|fatal|panic] regex replaces the old '-v error + non-empty stderr' check, so concealment warnings are no longer silently dropped. Regex shapes match ffmpeg showinfo output ('n:%4d pts:%7s pts_time:%-7s'; 'config in time_base: %d/%d'); greedy [^\n]* cannot mis-anchor on 'mean:' or 'duration:' because \bn: requires a word boundary. Extra or duplicate config lines (filter reconfig) and NOPTS frames both fail closed.

false_positives.basis: _relative_name charset excludes '\\', ':', whitespace, '%', and non-ASCII, so no drive letters, ADS, UNC, or percent-encoding; empty segments, '.', '..', trailing dots, and Windows device stems are rejected; the string is returned unmodified so downstream fullmatch on 'evidence/...png' sees the same bytes. load_snapshot additionally pins the asset set to manifest-derived names and rejects casefold collisions. No concrete bypass.

non_blocking_observations: audit.json 'extraction.log_sha256' is non-deterministic across re-runs: showinfo lines carry '@ 0x...' pointers and info-level progress/stats lines vary. Image SHAs are deterministic; the log hash is not. Consider -hide_banner -nostats, or hash only the parsed (n, pts, checksum) tuples.

The saved ffmpeg_showinfo.log now embeds absolute local paths (Input 'from ...', Output 'to ...') and the ffmpeg build banner. Acceptable for a private package, but new disclosure relative to ffprobe.json.
showinfo 'checksum'/'plane_checksum' of each raster is logged but not bound to the PNG sha256. Low value given lossless PNG in-process, but it is the one remaining unbound hop.
Any info-level line containing literal '[warning]' etc. (e.g. a clip filename) rejects the run. Fails closed; fine for the fixed three-clip scope.
Adversarial tests cover missing/shifted/reordered/clock/warning. Not covered: extra trailing observation, duplicate config lines, NOPTS. All fail closed by inspection.
PTS identity assumes decode_index rejects duplicate PTS within a clip; if it does not, two frames sharing a PTS would be indistinguishable to this check. Not verified from the supplied excerpt.
